name: National University
desc:
Records Evaluator I | $20.00-$23.00/hr | Records Review and Data Entry Heavy, Some Phone
Company: National University
Industry: Education and Training
What Your Day Will Look Like: You’d be the person at an online university who reviews student transcripts to decide which college credits count toward a degree. You’d look at courses students took at other schools, including foreign schools, military training, and credit-by-exam, and decide how each one applies to their program. Then you’d run and update each student’s degree audit (the checklist of what they still need to graduate) in the university’s system so it’s accurate. You’d also answer questions from students, advisors, and faculty about transfer credit and degree requirements, handle requests to change degree plans, and work with the other offices in the registrar’s area. It’s careful, detail-heavy record review work with regular contact by email and phone.
assessment: Yes, expect an assessment after applying or after initial contact with recruiter
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: No minimum education requirement is stated. A degree in tourism, hospitality, or a related field is a plus.
Required Experience: The posting asks for proven sales and negotiation skills and a track record of meeting or exceeding sales targets. It does not specify how many years of experience are required.
Preferred Experience: Familiarity with travel booking systems is an advantage. A tourism, hospitality, or related degree is a plus. The posting does not specify required years of travel industry experience.

Required Skills:
Strong knowledge of travel destinations, airlines, hotels, and travel products
Excellent verbal and written communication, active listening, and customer service
Sales, negotiation, and upselling skills
Ability to plan itineraries, coordinate bookings, manage budgets, and resolve problems
Attention to detail and ability to build client relationships
Advanced computer skills, including PowerPoint, PLEX, Executer, Word, Excel, and Outlook
Adaptability and flexibility to work evenings or weekends
Ability to work in a fast-paced, structured call center and meet sales and call goals

Best Fit: 
This role is ideal for someone who:
Knows travel destinations and enjoys helping people plan trips.
Has a strong customer service and sales background.
Is comfortable recommending additional services and working toward sales targets.
Can manage detailed bookings, use multiple computer programs, and adapt to flexible hours.
Not a Good Fit for someone who:
Dislikes sales, upselling, or performance targets.
Is uncomfortable handling customer calls in a structured call center.
Doesn’t enjoy detailed planning, booking coordination, or resolving travel problems.
Cannot work flexible hours, including evenings or weekends.
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process: 1. Application 2. Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you. 3. If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen. 4. If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview. Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.

Top 10 Resume Keywords:
• Records review and verification
• Accurate data entry
• Customer service
• Policy interpretation
• Problem solving
• Attention to detail
• Written and phone communication
• Confidentiality
• Multitasking and prioritizing
• Working independently and in a team
4-5 interview questions for this role:
• Tell us about your record keeping or customer service experience and how you keep details accurate.
• How would you explain a policy to a student who didn’t like the answer?
• Walk us through how you’d check a set of records against a list of requirements.
• How do you handle juggling several requests at once?
• Tell us about a time you solved a problem that didn’t have an obvious answer.

Notes: Bachelor’s degree is preferred, not required, and the posting says all skills, abilities, and education will be considered, so someone with a year of record keeping or customer service experience can apply. No travel is required. This role is a good way to build higher education and registrar experience.
Career Pathway: Not stated directly in posting, though the title “I” suggests levels within the role. Reasonable inferred path: Records Evaluator I → Records Evaluator II → Senior Records Evaluator → Registrar’s Office Supervisor, though this is an estimate, not confirmed by National University directly.
